# aibris v0.8.5

This release adds the first protected-content retention inventory, hardens the
scan cache and overlap accounting, and states the product boundary.

## Highlights

- `aibris scan` now inventories protected Codex session files
  (`~/.codex/sessions`) as a **read-only UTC-month aggregate**: a top-level
  `retention` JSON object (also shown in human output) with per-bucket
  unit/member counts, apparent bytes, and orphan statistics derived from
  proven-absent recorded working directories. The inventory never creates
  cleanup candidates, never selects or mutates members, and never blocks
  ordinary clean. The retention execution layer (selector, manifest,
  executor) stays parked. See `docs/PROTECTED_RETENTION.md` and
  `docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md`.
- The last-scan cache is now written atomically, so an interrupted scan cannot
  leave a partially written cache that a later `clean` would misread.
- Agent-state overlap accounting now derives fingerprint roots from the
  provider registry instead of a hardcoded list.
- Public docs now lead with agent state store cleanup; generic build debris is
  described as complementary coverage that keeps `scan` a complete picture.

## Notes

- The retention inventory is additive and non-authorizing: no member path,
  session identifier, or transcript content appears in the projection or its
  diagnostics, and retention rows never enter `summary` or cleanup
  eligibility.
- Safety contracts are unchanged: proof-based orphan eligibility, overlap hard
  locks, and the `--risky` boundary behave exactly as in v0.8.4.

## Windows status

Windows archives are **experimental**. The supported shape is the `amd64` /
`arm64` Windows zip archives cross-built by GoReleaser and listed in
`checksums.txt`. Native users verify the SHA-256 and place `aibris.exe` on the
PATH; `install.sh` remains Unix-only. Pull-request CI builds and exercises the
native executable (`--version`, `--help`, isolated `scan --json`), home /
cache isolation, recorded-cwd volume safety, and reparse-point cleanup
protection on `windows-latest`. A Windows version matrix is not published.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.8.5/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.
